commitResults.messageBody: Move user-facing printing into a Ui helper so Duke focuses more on command flow and persistence. Keep the behavior unchanged while updating the UI tests to match the LocalDate-based deadline and event formats, including ISO date inputs and saved-data loading expectations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract storage responsibilities into a dedicated class
commitResults.messageBody: Move file loading and saving into Storage so Duke no longer talks directly to Files or Path. Keep the command loop and task mutation behavior intact, and preserve the existing UI test coverage while the refactor remains behavior-preserving. This is the next small OOP step toward separating UI, storage, parsing, and task-list concerns.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command parsing into a parser class
commitResults.messageBody: Move user input splitting and command resolution out of Duke into Parser so the main loop only coordinates parsed results and task operations. Keep the observable behavior unchanged and preserve the existing UI coverage so this refactor remains a small, safe OOP step toward separate parser, storage, UI, and task-list responsibilities.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task list operations into a TaskList class
commitResults.messageBody: Move task mutation and access operations into TaskList so Duke no longer manipulates the underlying collection directly. This keeps the command loop focused on orchestration, while the task container now owns add, remove, mark, and size behavior. The refactor preserves the current UI behavior and keeps the design moving toward separate parser, storage, UI, and task-list responsibilities.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move task creation and validation into TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Teach TaskList to create task variants and validate indices so Duke no longer contains task-specific mutation logic. This keeps the main loop focused on orchestration while consolidating task collection behavior in one class. The UI test suite still passes unchanged, so the refactor preserves current behavior while making the object boundaries cleaner.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refine the object wiring for Duke and TaskList
commitResults.messageBody: Convert Duke into a small instance-based runner and let TaskList own persistence-triggered save calls. This trims the remaining static plumbing, keeps the command loop behavior unchanged, and makes the class boundaries a little cleaner after the earlier extractions. The UI tests still pass, so the change is a safe refinement rather than a behavioral shift.

Extract the command dispatch layer into concrete Command classes so parsing now returns executable objects instead of an enum-plus-switch pair. Duke becomes a smaller loop that reads input, asks the parser for a command, executes it, and checks whether the command exits. The UI tests were updated to reflect the new loop footer behavior, and the suite still passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize the project into Java packages
commitResults.messageBody: Add explicit duke, duke.command, duke.exception, duke.parser, duke.storage, duke.task, and duke.ui packages so the code matches the logical responsibilities already extracted. Keep src/main/java as the source root and preserve the current behavior while updating imports and package declarations throughout the codebase. The UI test suite still passes after the package split.

Move the application classes into package directories under src/main/java/duke while keeping a thin default-package launcher for existing scripts and tests. This keeps the source tree aligned with the package names without breaking the current UI test entry point.
